# Task P2-11: Soulseek source provider

**Phase:** 2 · **Depends on:** P2-01 (search runner), P2-02 (parser, quality), P2-10 (downloads) · **Suggested tier:** cheap worker · **Estimated size:** M

## Goal
The Soulseek source behind `ISourceProvider` (`src/Wondarr.Core/Sources/ISourceProvider.cs`): it turns a wanted song into a short, budget-aware sequence of Soulseek queries, maps every audio file slskd returns into a `Candidate`, stops early when the caller says the pool is good enough, and grabs / follows / cancels a chosen candidate through slskd's transfers. It makes **no** accept/reject decisions — that is the decision engine's job (P2-03) — and it does not enforce download timeouts (the queue tracker in Core does, P2-13b).

## Deliverables
Namespace `Wondarr.Sources.Slskd`.

1. `src/Wondarr.Sources.Slskd/SoulseekQueryBuilder.cs` — `static IReadOnlyList<string> Build(SongSearchRequest request)` returning the queries in order, de-duplicated case-insensitively (MATCHING_ENGINE §6.4, adapted — see "Why" below):
   1. `{main artist} {base title}{flag words}` — main artist = `request.MainArtists[0]` (fallback: `ArtistCredit` with any `feat.`/`ft.`/`featuring` clause removed); base title = `VersionFlagParser.Parse(request.Title).BaseTitle`; flag words = for each of `Live, Acoustic, Remix, Instrumental, Demo` present in `request.VersionFlags`, its wire name (`live`, `acoustic`, …) appended.
   2. The same text **folded**: `TextFolding.RemoveDiacritics` (existing, `src/Wondarr.Core/Metadata/TextFolding.cs`) — only when it differs from query 1.
   3. `{base title}{flag words}` alone — only when the normalised base title (`TextMatching.Normalize`) is at least 8 characters (a bare "One" or "Home" floods the network).
   4. `{main artist} {album title}` — only when `request.AlbumTitle` is set, is not `Singles` (the pseudo-album) and differs from the base title; Soulseek matches words against the **whole path**, so an album query returns the album folder's files including the wanted track.
   Every query is sanitised: characters `()[]{}"'!?.,:;&/\|*#+=~<>` become spaces; a token starting with `-` loses the `-` (a leading `-` excludes a word on Soulseek); whitespace collapsed; lower-cased; empty result dropped. **Why no `title artist` query and no `feat.`-stripped query:** Soulseek matches words regardless of order, and the base title already has `feat.` clauses removed, so both would repeat query 1 (record in the done-report if you disagree).
2. `src/Wondarr.Sources.Slskd/SoulseekCandidateMapper.cs` — `static IReadOnlyList<Candidate> Map(IReadOnlyList<SlskdSearchResponse> responses, string query)`: every entry of `files` (not `lockedFiles`) whose `SoulseekFilenameParser.Parse(filename).IsAudio` is true becomes a `Candidate` with `SourceType = SourceTypes.Soulseek`, `BlocklistKey = BlocklistKeys.Soulseek(username, filename)`, `DisplayName` = the last path segment, `RemotePath` = `filename` exactly as slskd sent it, `Provider` = `username`, `Parsed`, `Extension`, `DurationMs = length * 1000`, `BitrateKbps`, `SampleRate`, `BitDepth`, `IsVariableBitrate`, `SizeBytes`, `QualityId = SoulseekQuality.Infer(…)`, `Availability(hasFreeUploadSlot, queueLength, uploadSpeed)`, `IsLocked = file.isLocked`, `Query = query`. Duplicates by `BlocklistKey` keep the first.
3. *(removed: download timeouts live in Core's `QueueOptions`, P2-13b, because the queue tracker in Core enforces them)*
4. `src/Wondarr.Sources.Slskd/SoulseekSourceProvider.cs` — `sealed class SoulseekSourceProvider : ISourceProvider` (singleton), constructor `(ISlskdSearchRunner, ISlskdDownloads, SlskdStatus, IOptionsMonitor<SoulseekOptions>, ILogger<SoulseekSourceProvider>)`:
   - `SourceType` = `soulseek`.
   - `GetAvailabilityAsync`: `Mode == External` → `(false, "External slskd mode arrives in Phase 5")`; no credentials → `(false, "Soulseek is not configured")`; status not `Running` or not reachable → `(false, "slskd is not running")`; not logged in → `(false, "Soulseek: not logged in")`; else `(true, null)`.
   - `SearchAsync`: if not available → empty result with the reason as `Message` (no search submitted). Otherwise run the queries of item 1 **sequentially** through `ISlskdSearchRunner.RunAsync` (the runner enforces the global budget — never bypass it), map, merge (de-duplicate by `BlocklistKey` across queries, first wins), and after each query call `request.IsPoolGoodEnough?.Invoke(allCandidatesSoFar)` — `true` stops the sequence. `SlskdSearchRejectedException` (slskd's own 429) ends the sequence with what was collected and `Message` "slskd refused a search (too many in flight)". `OperationCanceledException` propagates. Any other exception from one query is logged (Warning) and the next query still runs; if every query failed, `Message` = "Soulseek search failed: <first error message>". `Queries` = the texts actually submitted.
   - `GrabAsync(candidate, destination)`: requires `SourceType == soulseek`, a `Provider` and a `SizeBytes`; `ISlskdDownloads.EnqueueAsync(candidate.Provider, candidate.RemotePath, size, destination, externalId: destination)` → `GrabHandle("soulseek", JsonSerializer.Serialize(slskdGrab))` (camelCase).
   - `GetStatusAsync(handle)`: deserialize the grab, `ISlskdDownloads.GetStatusAsync`, map: `Requested`, `Initializing`, `Queued|Locally` → `Queued`; `Queued|Remotely` → `RemotelyQueued` (with `PlaceInQueue`); `InProgress` → `Downloading`; `Completed|Succeeded` with a `LocalPath` → `Completed` (`CompletedPath` = it, `Progress` 1); `Completed|Succeeded` without one → `Failed` with the slskd-downloads error; `Completed` with `Cancelled` → `Cancelled`; `Completed` with `Errored`/`Rejected`/`TimedOut`/`Aborted` → `Failed` with `Message` = "Soulseek transfer <rejected|errored|timed out|aborted>: <slskd exception text if any>". `Progress` = `PercentComplete / 100`.
   - `CancelAsync(handle)` → `ISlskdDownloads.CancelAsync`; exceptions are logged and swallowed (idempotent).
5. Register `ISourceProvider` → `SoulseekSourceProvider` (singleton; `services.AddSingleton<ISourceProvider, SoulseekSourceProvider>()` so later sources add more implementations) in `AddWondarrSlskd`.
6. Tests in `tests/Wondarr.Sources.Tests/Slskd/`:
   - `SoulseekQueryBuilderTests` — Get Lucky (`["Daft Punk"]`, "Get Lucky", album "Random Access Memories") → exactly `["daft punk get lucky", "get lucky", "daft punk random access memories"]` ("get lucky" normalises to 9 characters, so the title-only query is included); Sigur Rós "Hoppípolla" → folded second query `sigur ros hoppipolla`; a live song adds `live`; "One" by U2 → no title-only query; `Singles` album → no album query; `AC/DC` sanitised; a title token `-ish` loses the `-`; `feat.` credit fallback.
   - `SoulseekCandidateMapperTests` — over the **recorded** `tests/fixtures/slskd/live/search-responses.json`: every non-audio file (`.lrc`, `.cue`, `.jpg`, `.log`, `.sfk`, `syno_dtime`) is dropped, locked files are not mapped, keys are unique, and a spot-check of one FLAC and one MP3 candidate's fields (take them from the fixture).
   - `SoulseekSourceProviderTests` — fakes for the runner and downloads: availability reasons; queries run in order and stop when `IsPoolGoodEnough` returns true after the first; merge de-duplicates; one failing query does not stop the next; slskd 429 stops with the message; unavailable → no search at all; the state mapping table of item 4 (one case per row); grab builds the handle and a round-trip through `GetStatusAsync` reads it back.

## Acceptance criteria (each must be demonstrated)
1. `dotnet build -warnaserror` → 0 warnings, 0 errors; `dotnet test` → all pass (paste the summary lines).
2. The mapper test over the recorded responses passes; the query-builder cases pass.
3. The state-mapping cases pass, one per row of item 4.

## Out of scope
- Scoring, persistence, grabbing policy, download timeouts (P2-12/P2-13), the hub, browsing user folders.
